name: Granby Roll to Guard
summary: The turtled player rolls across the shoulder and upper back, keeps weight off the neck, and reinserts the legs to recover facing closed or open guard under controlled contact.
description: The turtled player rolls across the shoulder and upper back, keeps weight off the neck, and reinserts the legs to recover facing closed or open guard under controlled contact.
overview:
The turtled player rolls across the shoulder and upper back, keeps weight off the neck, and reinserts the legs to recover facing closed or open guard under controlled contact.

Begin on the knees and forearms in Turtle/Bottom, underneath or alongside the opponent's controlling ride. Check that the head and rolling shoulder can move safely before beginning the recovery.

Roll diagonally across the shoulder and upper back rather than planting the head or loading the neck. Bring the hips through the available space while keeping the neck unloaded and the knees free to move. Face the opponent and bring the knees back between the bodies as the rolling space opens. Settle Closed Guard/Bottom when the ankles can close comfortably, or facing Open Guard/Bottom when they cannot.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.

defender.name: Granby Roll to Guard Defender
defender.description: Recognize Granby Roll to Guard and interrupt its required connections before the final control is established.
defender.overview:
You oppose the performer of this action. Follow the controlled roll while maintaining a stable and balanced base. Keep the recovering player's neck free of stacked body weight. Address the returning knees before guard is established. Recognize Turtle if the roll is interrupted before guard recovery. Claim rear control only when its actual torso and leg connections exist.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.

flashcards.answer: Follow the controlled roll while maintaining a stable and balanced base.

flashcards.question: Against Granby Roll to Guard, when must you stop moving?
flashcards.answer: Stop at a tap, verbal signal, distress, or a loaded joint or neck. Release before changing direction.

flashcards.question: Against Granby Roll to Guard, does interrupting one grip guarantee a new position?
flashcards.answer: No. Confirm the remaining body and leg controls before claiming the guard, pin, or submission has changed.
